title: Acute Respiratory Distress Evaluation
description: Evaluation of dyspnea, wheezing, and acute hypoxia with immediate emergency stratification.

risk_rules.name: Severe Respiratory Distress / Impending Respiratory Failure
risk_rules.reason: Patient is unable to speak in full sentences due to breathlessness, reports bluish discoloration of lips/fingers (cyanosis), or high-pitched stridor indicating upper airway obstruction.
risk_rules.possible_concern: Acute respiratory failure / Critical airway compromise

risk_rules.name: Anaphylaxis with Respiratory Involvement
risk_rules.reason: Acute shortness of breath developing rapidly after exposure to food/medication/insect sting accompanied by lip/tongue swelling, hives, or throat tightness.

risk_rules.name: Acute Asthma or COPD Exacerbation
risk_rules.reason: Audible wheezing, persistent chest tightness, and breathlessness with incomplete relief from rescue inhaler.

risk_rules.name: Productive Cough with Exertional Breathlessness
risk_rules.reason: Shortness of breath accompanied by fever, productive cough with colored phlegm, or pleuritic chest discomfort.
risk_rules.possible_concern: Lower respiratory tract infection (Bronchitis or Pneumonia)

risk_rules.name: Mild Upper Airway Congestion
risk_rules.reason: Mild breathlessness attributed to nasal congestion or seasonal rhinitis without wheezing, chest pain, or exertion limitation.
risk_rules.possible_concern: Upper respiratory viral illness / Allergic rhinitis

possible_conditions.name: Acute respiratory compromise / Severe asthma
possible_conditions.reason_template: Severe shortness of breath, wheezing, or difficulty completing sentences.
possible_conditions.caveat: Immediate evaluation and objective pulse oximetry / nebulizer therapy required.

possible_conditions.name: Lower respiratory tract infection / Pneumonia
possible_conditions.reason_template: Breathlessness coupled with fever, chills, and purulent sputum or localized crackles.
possible_conditions.caveat: Physician evaluation recommended for auscultation and chest radiography.

possible_conditions.name: Pulmonary embolism
possible_conditions.reason_template: Sudden onset of dyspnea, tachycardia, or unilateral pleuritic pain.
possible_conditions.caveat: Requires clinical evaluation and D-dimer / CT pulmonary angiography if risk criteria met.

recommended_questions.safety_relevance: Most immediate bedside triage indicator of critical respiratory reserve.
recommended_questions.question: Can you speak a full sentence comfortably without having to stop for air?

recommended_questions.safety_relevance: Identifies dangerous hypoxemia or upper airway stridor.
recommended_questions.question: Are your lips, face, or fingernails turning blue or pale, or are you making a high-pitched squeaking noise when breathing in?

recommended_questions.safety_relevance: Screens for life-threatening anaphylactic airway compromise.
recommended_questions.question: Do you notice any swelling of your lips, tongue, or throat, or any sudden itching and hives?

recommended_questions.safety_relevance: Differentiates primary lung disease from cardiopulmonary emergencies (PE, pneumothorax, ACS).
recommended_questions.question: Are you also experiencing chest pain, tightness, or a racing heartbeat?
